sweep_summary: taha1241 (Tahaggart Tamahaq) is not in the catalog. The single title-works with stress in the title, Aikhenvald & Nientao 1988 'On accent in Tamasheq' (Russian, 3 pp., Moscow postgraduate conference volume), is confirmed to exist by Aikhenvald's own CV (saved:, p.24) but no copy or abstract is reachable online; its variety is unclear (the Russian 'tamashek' is generic Tuareg and the Malian co-author suggests Mali Tamasheq, taq, rather than Ahaggar), so relevance is unclear and acquisition priority medium (print only in Russia). The best first-hand statement actually read is Prasse 1972, Manuel de grammaire touaregue (tahaggart), pp. 30-37 (already held by the project, page images verified against the scanned): a non-contrastive pitch accent, penultimate by default for nouns/verbs of <=3 syllables, antepenultimate for trisyllabic nouns with light or geminate-closed penult ending in a vowel and for plural types 2/3/4/7 (Ahaggar and Aïr, not Iwellemmeden), final for masculine numerals and long-final intensive perfects, with many rules flagged as provisional. Vycichl & Chaker 1984 (Encyclopédie berbère 'Accent') is a consistent second-hand summary of Prasse. only direct downloads and APIs were used. updated (addendum).

new_statements.translation: [p.30] The place of the main accent and the kind of rhythm required appear to depend on the quantitative syllable structure of each accentual unit, but in a rather complicated way [...] Accent therefore has no phonological function. There are no pairs of words distinguished solely by (the place of) the accent. [p.32] a) 'Hollow rhythm' with accent on the antepenult is required by: (1) trisyllabic singular nouns whose penult is short or closed by a geminate and which end in a vowel, e.g. áġənnà 'sky' [...] c) 'Even rhythm' with accent on the penult is required by: (1) all nouns, sg. or pl., of 3 syllables or fewer, except those of § a [...] [p.33] (2) all verbs of 3 syllables or fewer without a long vowel [...]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tahaggart has a non-contrastive, mainly musical (pitch) word accent. In isolated words the main accent falls on the penult by default for nouns and verbs of up to three syllables; it retracts to the antepenult under quantity/morphological conditions (trisyllabic sg. nouns with light or geminate-closed penult ending in a vowel, penult closed by a geminate, certain plural classes, nouns of >3 syllables with a long antepenult, verbs with long antepenult vowel); intensive verb forms accent their first long vowel; masculine numerals 1-10 and a few verb forms with long final vowel are final-accented. In enclitic groups the accent tends to shift to the syllable adjacent to the clitic. Prasse stresses the rules are provisional ('n'est connu que dans ses grandes lignes').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Three degrees distinguished: principal (high tone, slight dynamic increase), secondary (mid tone), tertiary (low tone); normal 'rythme égal' rises to the main accent and falls after it (3-2-1-2-3), while 'rythme creux' places a tertiary syllable adjacent to the main accent (2-3-1-3-2); Prasse marks principal with acute and tertiary with grave (e.g. áġənnà).
new_statements.exceptions: Numerals 1-10 masc. final (əssín, səmmús); kălá 'non' final; intensive perfects accent the long vowel (iktâb final); dialect differences: Y follows Ahaggar for plurals like íkəbrân but WE/WW/N say ikə́brân; several sub-rules explicitly marked 'sujette à des vérifications ultérieures'; possible accent displacement under emphasis (p.37).
new_statements.domain_note: Rules stated for 'mots autonomes à l'état isolé' (citation forms); the accentual unit may be a word or an enclitic group with one main accent, with separate rules (§B.3, pp. 34-37) for accent placement and shift in enclitic groups; accent is independent of poetic metre, which is quantity-based.
new_statements.identity_note: Prasse 1972 describes the tăhăggart dialect (Kel-Ahaggar, Tamanrasset), i.e. exactly taha1241, based mainly on Foucauld's Ahaggar materials plus Prasse's own 1958 notes; he flags dialect differences in accent for Y (Ayer), WE/WW (Tawellemmet, Niger/Mali) and N, which are other glottocodes (e.g. tama1365 Tamasheq, tawa1286/ayer varieties) and should not be conflated.

new_statements.translation: It is essentially a musical (pitch) accent with little dynamic variation. [...] The accent therefore has no phonological function; there are no word pairs distinguished solely by (the position of) the accent. [...] (a) The 'hollow rhythm' with accent on the antepenult is required by: (1) trisyllabic singular nouns whose penult is short or closed by a geminate and which end in a vowel [...] (c) The 'even rhythm' with accent on the penult is required by: (1) all nouns, sg. or pl., of 3 syllables or fewer, except those under (a).
new_statements.citation: Prasse, Karl-G. 1972. Manuel de grammaire touaregue (tahaggart), I-III: Phonetique - Ecriture - Pronom. Copenhague: Akademisk Forlag, pp. 30-33 (Ch. I, B 'L'accent', 1 Généralités; 2 L'accent des mots isolés).
new_statements.reading: Tahaggart word accent is a non-contrastive pitch accent whose position is predictable from syllable quantity and morphological class: default penultimate (nouns and long-vowel-less verbs of <=3 syllables), antepenultimate when the penult is light/geminate-closed and the word ends in a vowel, in several plural types (Ahaggar/Aïr-specific), and in longer nouns with a heavy antepenult; final in masculine numerals 1-10 and in intensive perfects with a long final vowel; intensives accent the first lengthened vowel; clitic groups re-align accent. Prasse himself flags the polysyllable rules as provisional. For a catalog's classification this is a quantity-sensitive, morphologically conditioned system with penultimate as the unmarked position, not a fixed-position system.

B 'L'accent' pp. 30-37: musical accent with three degrees (principal = high tone + slight dynamic increase; secondary; tertiary); no phonological function (no minimal pairs by accent place); placement in isolated words depends on quantitative syllable structure and word class: nouns and verbs of <=3 syllables take penult accent ('rythme égal'), trisyllabic sg. nouns with short/geminate-closed penult ending in a vowel or penult closed by a geminate and certain plural types take antepenult ('rythme creux'), nouns of >3 syllables with long antepenult take antepenult, intensive verbs…

sources.quote: Quant au touareg, les anciens auteurs ne parlent pas de l'accent. Mais Karl-G. Prasse traite le problème de l'accent en touareg dans ses « Notes sur la langue touarègue » (Acta Orientalia, XXV, 1959, p. 43-111). Le même sujet est repris augmenté dans son Manuel de grammaire touarègue, Copenhague, 1972, vol. 1, p. 30-37. [...] Les Touaregs du Hoggar et de l'Aïr disent íkәbrān « huttes », íhănān « tentes » [...] Certains mots sont accentués sur la pénultième : abáyoγ « outre », akátab « écriture ».
sources.note: Second-hand: §7-8 summarize Prasse 1959 (Acta Orientalia 25: 43-111) and Prasse 1972 vol. 1 pp. 30-37 -- three accent degrees, no phonological function, complicated rules, 3-2-1-2-3 rhythm, examples áġənnà 'ciel', some words penult (abáyoġ, akátab), ámis vs səmmús; notes Hoggar/Aïr íkəbrān vs Iwellemmeden ikə́brān.

sources.note: Title-only: a 3-page Russian conference abstract on accent in 'Tamasheq'. Glottolog attaches it to four Tuareg languages (thv, ttq, taq, thz); the Russian label 'тамашек' is generic for Tuareg, and the co-author's surname (Nientao) is Malian, so the data are plausibly Malian Tamasheq (taq) rather than Ahaggar Tahaggart. Aikhenvald's CV lists fieldwork 'Tashelhit, Kabyle and Tamachek, 1981-1988'. No copy found: Crossref, Google Books API and archive.org return nothing; HathiTrust catalog behind a JS challenge; her website lists only 2003+ publications with PDFs. Print-only in Russian libraries…
